content.text: {"headline":"Recommend no action: Payments is predicted to recover to 81.2% (target 80%) over 15:30-19:45 without any changes, at no extra cost.","why":"The surge is most likely from the 10:55 reward-points email to 500,000 card holders. Payments calls ran +52% at 11:30 (164 vs 108 expected) and service level fell to 32%, with the extra calls coming in mostly as other_payments (1.77x) and refund_status (1.56x). Confidence in the cause is medium because the email is about card rewards rather than Payments & UPI directly. For the disruption window (15:30-19:45), doing nothing is predicted to give 85.6% overall, with Payments at 81.2% and General at 96.4%, and 4.5% abandons. That meets the 80% target at ₹0, so it is the cheapest plan within policy. Rest-of-day is predicted at 85.7%. No escalation is needed.","trade_offs":["P1 (no-cost cross-skilled moves plus late callback) also costs ₹0 and gives the same 85.6% overall. It lifts Payments only to 81.3% and trims abandons to 4.1%, while General dips slightly to 96.1%. It means more disruption for almost no gain.","P3 (strongest compliant plan, ₹900) gives more headroom: Payments 85.4%, 88.8% overall and 2.8% abandons. It is worth considering if you want a safety margin over the 80% target.","P2 performs best (Payments 91.0%, 2.0% abandons, ₹804) but breaks policy CX-01. It uses a known-issue IVR message without a confirmed outage or incident, so it should not be used."],"watch":"Payments is only about 1 point above target under no action, so watch it closely. If Payments service level is tracking below 80% or abandons rise above about 4.5%, switch to P3 (₹900). Also check whether the campaign calls keep growing beyond the forecast."}
